newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH PM SAYS FLOOD BONDS TO BE LAUNCHED AUG 1.
newsitem.headline: CZECH PM SAYS FLOOD BONDS TO BE LAUNCHED AUG 1.

text.p: Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said on Tuesday that bonds aimed at raising funds for flood relief programmes will have a maturity of five years, and a net yield which "roughly covers" inflation.

"Our intention is to find a value which would mean that net yield, after taxation, roughly covers inflation," he said adding the coupon would not be fixed. Klaus said he expected the bonds to be launched on August 1.

Klaus told journalists after a meeting of economic ministers that the bonds would be issued in material fomr, though the government was also considering issuing them in book form for institutional investors.
Last week, parliament approved the issuance of up to five billion crowns in bonds to raise emergency funds for flood relief in the eastern part of the country.
Klaus did not say how much of the five billion crown limit the government would use.
For over a week, the eastern part of the Czech Republic has suffered the worst flooding this century caused damage estimated at as much as 100 billion crowns, killing at least 39 people.
The flood interrupted rail and road connections in the affected regions as well as gas, power and telephone links.
The Czech parliament has also approved the release of up to another five billion from privatisation proceeds to help with the relief programme.
